findings.explanation: `/api/admin/history/v1/conference/` holds only conferences that are no longer in progress. Its `participant_count` is the total number of participant calls over the whole conference, with reconnects counted twice, not a concurrent count. Summing it per time bucket does not give concurrent participants, so the utilisation figure would be wrong.
findings.quote: Calculate utilization as total concurrent participants divided by capacity. Use `predict` to forecast peak demand 24 hours ahead. Alert when utilization exceeds 80%
findings.suggested_fix: Explain that history records describe completed conferences. Either derive concurrency from participant history start/end times (for example with the `concurrency` command or interval expansion), or poll the live status API (`/api/admin/status/v1/participant/`) for real-time concurrency. State that `participant_count` counts total calls, including reconnects.

findings.explanation: The 10,000 figure is the Management Node's retention limit, not a response size. Responses are paginated (default 20 objects). A plain 5-minute poll would either return only the first page or re-index the same retained records on every run unless the script filters and checkpoints.
findings.quote: polls the Pexip Management REST API at `/api/admin/history/v1/conference/` every 5 minutes. The API returns up to 10,000 conference instances
findings.suggested_fix: Describe paginated collection (`limit`/`offset`, `order_by=-start_time` or an `end_time__gte=<checkpoint>` filter) with a checkpoint, so each completed conference is indexed once. Note that history keeps only the most recent 10,000 conferences.

findings.explanation: The conference history record (name, start_time, end_time, duration, participant_count, service_type, tag, participants) has no node pool or location field to join on. The capacity lookup has no key in this feed.
findings.quote: Build a `pexip_capacity_lookup` CSV mapping node pools to their maximum participant capacity.
findings.suggested_fix: Key capacity on a field the data actually has. Look up whether participant history (`/api/admin/history/v1/participant/`) exposes the system location or conferencing node per call and join there, or document a single platform-wide capacity value.

findings.explanation: In implementation and description, the alert depends on utilisation and on a predicted-peak vs capacity comparison. The SPL's final `timechart` keeps only avg/peak participants, and `predict` outputs a forecast with no capacity comparison. No alertable condition exists in the search.
findings.quote: Alert when utilization exceeds 80% or when predicted peaks will exceed capacity.
findings.suggested_fix: Either describe the UC as a capacity-trending report with no alert, or state the exact alert condition the search must output (for example predicted upper bound > max_capacity) once the SPL carries it.

findings.explanation: The generic scripted-input stanza contradicts the UC's own `index=pexip` and `sourcetype=pexip:conference_history`, and its echo script does not call the Pexip API.
findings.suggested_fix: Show a stanza with `index = pexip` and `sourcetype = pexip:conference_history`, and describe a script that calls the history endpoint with pagination and a checkpoint, emitting one JSON event per conference.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: Does not measure concurrency. It bins completed-conference records by `_time` and sums `participant_count` (total calls per conference), and the `start`/`end` epochs it computes are never used. The `lookup pexip_capacity_lookup node_pool` runs after `stats ... by _time` has dropped all fields except _time, so max_capacity and utilization_pct are always null, and the final timechart discards utilization_pct anyway. Use participant start/end times with `concurrency`, or the status API, and join capacity on a field that exists. Evidence: https://docs.pexip.com/api_manage/api_history.htm
'high' is generous for a capacity-trending report built on retrospective CDRs with no working alert condition.

summary: The Pexip history API path is real, but the UC treats completed-conference CDRs as a live concurrency feed and `participant_count` as concurrent participants. It also maps capacity by a node-pool field the conference record does not carry, so the utilisation and 80% alert it describes cannot be produced.
